highlights.title: Pakistan investigating 'discipline and conduct' in latest twist on crisis tour
highlights.summary: The Pakistan Cricket Board has launched an investigation into "media reports concerning discipline and conduct" amid the team's crisis tour of England.
body: Pakistan last week took the unprecedented step of sending seven players home and calling up seven after losing heavily at Headingley and Lord's to fall 2-0 down in the three-match series.

Head coach Sarfaraz Ahmed and assistant Umar Gul have also been replaced, with Mike Hesson, in charge of Pakistan's white-ball sides, and former Australia seamer Ashley Noffke overseeing the third Test at Edgbaston, which begins on Wednesday.
A statement read: "The Pakistan Cricket Board has initiated an internal disciplinary inquiry following media reports concerning discipline and conduct, which are currently being reviewed internally.
"The PCB handles such matters in accordance with its standard procedures. The process is being conducted under PCB regulations, ensuring that all concerned individuals are given due consideration.

highlights.title: Whispering Complaints Into Your Phone May Be the Future of Customer Feedback
highlights.summary: Forget email surveys or long calls spent on hold. Voicebox lets people send customer feedback by recording a voice note on their phone.
body: Some of the hottest software this year revolves around capturing voices. Whether it’s the sharp dictations of Wispr or the always-listening ears of Granola, voice-centered software currently feels inescapable. Voice dictation is getting so sharp, in fact, that I often write drafts in my notepad and then dictate aloud to my laptop.

Some prognosticators have declared this to be a dramatic end-of-the-keyboard moment, where legions of white-collar workers will soon be quietly whispering into desk microphones rather than clacking away at keyboards. I disagree, but I do think these changes could upend how customers give feedback.

I rarely email customer support unless something substantially negative has happened and I’m fishing for a refund. I’m much more open to giving feedback by blabbering for 20 seconds into my phone, good or bad, than I am to waiting on hold for who knows how long until someone answers.

highlights.title: Patrice Désilets vows to make a sequel to Ancestors: The Humankind Odyssey
highlights.summary: Patrice Désilets, the creator of the Assassin's Creed series and director of 1666: Amsterdam, has said he will make a sequel to open-world human evolution survival game Ancestors: The Humankind Odyssey.
body: Désilets, talking to me at a recent 1666: Amsterdam event, said 2019's Ancestors: The Humankind Odyssey was written as a "volume one". "I've designed different volumes to eventually be growing the game," he said.
I didn't think he owned the Ancestors franchise - I thought Take-Two's defunct publishing label Private Division did. However, Désilets replied: "I own the IP. But it's complex."

So he could make a sequel if he wanted to. "Yeah," he confirmed. "I will. I will. And people can believe me because I'm ready to wait 16 fucking years to finish what I started [with 1666 Amsterdam]; I finish what I started."

Ancestors: The Humankind Odyssey was an imaginative concept, a game that charted humankind's evolution from primate into upright walking human, across millions of years of time. As a player, you survived through different eras of third-person action survival gameplay, as the game lurched millions of years through time.

highlights.title: Betty Gilpin Jabs at Sam Altman During ‘Manic Poem’ Acceptance Speech at the Emmys
highlights.summary: “Widow’s Bay” guest star Betty Gilpin accepted her Emmy win for outstanding guest actress in a comedy by reading a poem she had written in jest — and very much in the unique style of the show. But it was one line that especially got the TV Academy audience at the Peacock Theatre to cheer:
body: “Thank you, Cosmo. My family, my daughters, friends — too many to name — my brothers Sam, Harry and my long dead dog Babe. Thank you.”
Where did the idea for the poem come from? Gilpin credited her episodic co-star Hamish Linklater, who also earned a guest actor in a comedy Emmy nomination for playing Richard Warren.

“I was on the same flight over as my co-nominee Hamish Linklater, and he came over to my row and was like, ‘Have you written a speech?’ And I was like, ‘Oh no, no, no! I’m not going to win,’” she said. “He’s like, ‘Well, you need to do that because it’s a scientific possibility, and don’t be stupid. Just prepare something.’ So he scared the shit out of me, and I wrote a quick manic poem, as you know, women have done for centuries. And I love my dog Babe. I named my first daughter after him. I’m almost ready for a dog, decade away.”
“Widow’s Bay” ended Night 2 of the 78th Emmys with eight wins — the most of any program so far. Gilpin called the recognition “incredible.”

highlights.title: My favorite family heirloom: an old Zojirushi hot water dispenser better than any tea kettle
highlights.summary: It heats water up fast and crucially, keeps it warm for the whole day, so you can can access hot water to your heart’s content. Sign up for the Filter US newsletter, your weekly guide to buying fewer, better things.
body: O f all the things my mother has given me from the vast warehouse of her garage, there are two items I treasure the most. One, a Costco-sized box of gallon-sized Ziploc bags, and two, a battered Zojirushi water boiler that has been in the family for decades. The Ziploc bags are nice to have and can be easily replaced; the water boiler, on the other hand, has become an indispensable tool that makes my life at home a little better, every time I use it.

A brief twist: if given the choice, I’d take an ice cold beverage over hot any time. But even I, with my preference for drinks so cold that they hurt my teeth, have been converted to my family’s beloved Zojirushi.

I use it almost every day – for the instant Cafe Bustelo coffee that I drink every morning, for instant noodles, for tea and hot chocolate and any other wintry weather beverage. Once you’ve opened your heart (and wallet) to one of these things, I promise you that you will never look back.

highlights.title: Farrell on retirement, fond memories, and next steps with Wigan
highlights.summary: Wigan Warriors captain Liam Farrell says he is not sure if he will play for the club again after he announced he will retireat the end of the 2026 Super League season.
body: The 36-year-old, who has only ever played for the Warriors, will call time on a career which has spanned 17 professional seasons. Farrell has captained Wigan since 2023 and been capped 12 times by England.
He has totalled 428 appearances for Wigan and scored 151 tries, winning six Super League titles, five Challenge Cups and two World Club Challenge successes during his illustrious career.

Farrell has not featured since June with an ongoing neck issue and with just three potential matches remaining in the season for his club, the chances of him featuring again for his boyhood club are in doubt.
That third match, if Wigan were to make it, would be the Super League Grand Final at Old Trafford on October 3, live on Sky Sports.

highlights.title: Alienware Just Released the World's First 39" 5K Monitor With RGB Stripe Tandem OLED Technology
highlights.summary: Earlier this year, Dell announced the "world's first 39" 5K monitor with RGB stripe tandem OLED technology." You can finally get your hands on one. The new Alienware AW3926QW has just been listed at Dell for $1,099.99 with free delivery (10% less if you have a verified student account).
body: The Alienware AW3926QW has no lack of features that make it stand out from the crowd, but perhaps its most impressive technology is the RGB stripe tandem OLED panel. Tandem OLED stacks multiple OLED layers on top of each other instead of a single layer. Tandem OLED is better than other OLED panels because: 1) it's much brighter (the AW3926QW in particular has a very impressive 1,300 nits of peak brightness) and 2) it's less prone to burn-in.

The AW3926QW doubles down on this with new RGB stripe technology. Whereas traditional tandem OLEDs use white pixels, RGB stripe tandem OLED breaks the color down further into vertically aligned red, green, and blue pixels. This reduces color fringing and in turn significantly improves text clarity. It goes without saying that there are obvious benefits here for both gaming and productivity purposes alike.

highlights.title: Film Industry Leaders Demand Structural Fix for Gender Gap at Lumiere Summit
highlights.summary: Women held 17% of key behind-camera roles when the Celluloid Ceiling study began tracking the figure in 1998. Last year, that number stood at 23%. Six points in 27 years.
body: Berlinale festival director Tricia Tuttle cited her own festival’s data. In 2005, women directed 0% of films in Berlinale competition. By 2015 that had reached 15%, and by 2025 it stood at 40%. “Transparency makes you very aware, as a curator and as a decision-maker and a cultural gatekeeper, of what you’re doing,” Tuttle said. She added that data consistently shows films made with greater gender balance perform better commercially. “That’s a lot of creative energy that gets wasted,” Tuttle said, referring to the effort women are forced to spend justifying the conversation rather than making work.

highlights.title: Grindr pays £26m to settle UK lawsuit over allegedly sharing users’ HIV status
highlights.summary: US-owned dating app allegedly allowed ad firms access to private information in breach of UK law. Business live – latest updates. Grindr will pay £26m to settle a lawsuit brought by thousands of users in the UK who allege that the US dating app shared highly sensitive personal information…
body: The settlement brings to an end a two-year legal battle, after the UK law firm Austen Hays filed a claim at the high court of England and Wales in April 2024 on behalf of Grindr users alleging violations of UK privacy laws during a period up to early 2020.
The London law firm represented 12,000 people, who will receive an average compensation of £2,167 each, if the £26m is equally distributed.

Grindr was founded in 2009 to make it easier to coordinate hookups for gay men. It now claims to be the world’s largest dating app for gay, bi, trans and queer people, with nearly 15 million users around the world.

Grindr said in a US regulatory filing that it had resolved the UK group action related to what it described as “historical data practices before 2020”, when Grindr was owned and controlled by the Chinese gaming company Beijing Kunlun Tech.

highlights.title: Six years later, Sony revisits its legendary XM4 headphones
highlights.summary: Six years ago Sony and Bose were in the middle of a noise-canceling battle, with each new model of headphones better than the last. In the fall of 2020, Sony released the WH-1000XM4 headphones to wide acclaim.
body: After the WH-1000XM4 were discontinued in 2025, Sony is bringing them back as the WH-1000XM4C.

The XM4C look identical to the original XM4 (although they now have a lavender option), with the same hinge design and ability to fold up. It’s a compact design that Sony moved away from when it released the XM5 in 2022, and then returned to (although not quite as compact) with the XM6. But it’s not just the look that’s returned. The XM4C still use the same QN1 processing chip and four microphones for ANC. That design is showing its age: The XM5 still used the QN1, but had eight mics. Last year’s XM6 have 12, plus the new QN3 chip.

Sony did update the XM4C’s sound profile to bring it in line with current models, and the headphones have a 10-band EQ in the Headphones app, instead of the 5-band on the XM4, plus a gaming preset. The XM4C also support Bluetooth 6 instead of 5. Surprisingly, the battery performance on the new headphones is slightly worse. Sony claims the XM4C get up to 27 hours of use with ANC on as opposed to 30 hours previously. Not a huge difference, and still more than enough for a cross-country trip.

highlights.title: The pet I’ll never forget: Harold, the halls of residence cat, who looked after me when I first left home
highlights.summary: He was the gorgeous furry tabby who made my day, even when he waltzed into my flat just to finish my takeaway. Now he’s a campus celeb, with a part-time job guarding the doors of the village shop.
body: I n 2022, when I moved into halls of residence at the University of Sheffield, my biggest concern was no longer having a furry friend to come home to, as I’d had a cat since I was 11 years old. Then I met Harold.

My first encounter with this gorgeous tabby was quite unusual. One day, in our 10-bed flat, a flurry of messages appeared on the group WhatsApp chat after my fellow roommates caught an intruder on the sofa, innocently munching on my leftover pizza.

As in many homes for first year university students, there were plenty of unfinished takeaways lying around the kitchen. And Harold was a smart cat with a clear goal: food. Any time he saw a snack or sensed one from a distance, he would come running. A can of tuna. A block of cheese. The occasional pancake. And I was more than happy to feed him – he probably had a better diet than me.
points: He was the gorgeous furry tabby who made my day, even when he waltzed into my flat just to finish my takeaway.

highlights.title: Authors push back as publishers and agents make claims on Anthropic settlement
highlights.summary: Authors say publishers seem to be claiming more than their fair share of settlement payments.
body: Some authors hoping to receive their share of Anthropic’s $1.5 billion copyright settlement said they received surprising emails this week — emails informing them that someone else was making a claim on their payments.

Anthropic settled a copyright class action suit last year, after a judge ruled that training AI models on copyrighted material is legal under fair use doctrine, but pirating that material was not. The deal received final approval in July, allowing the payments to move forward.

Under the terms of the settlement, the authors of nearly 500,000 titles will be paid $3,000 for each pirated work. If the book is still in-print with a traditional publisher, the money will be split 50-50 between author and publisher. If the book was self-published, or if the publisher reverted the rights by allowing the book to go out-of-print, then the author should get the entire payment.
points: Authors say publishers seem to be claiming more than their fair share of settlement payments.

highlights.title: ‘Mistrust’ of Palantir may affect NHS research, says health minister
highlights.summary: James Frith says patients may be less willing to share data as new figures show a rise in opt-outs. Concern is being raised about Palantir’s work with the NHS as new figures showed tens of thousands of patients have withdrawn their data from use in research projects.
body: James Frith, the health innovation minister, said he was worried about “mistrust” of the US defence and health tech company and “the impact it could have on people’s willingness to share data with the NHS”.
The government is deciding whether to axe the company’s £330m contract to operate the health service’s federated data platform, which is intended to improve efficiency and patient outcomes.

Frith’s comment, in a letter to Layla Moran, the chair of the Commons health committee, follows a rise in patients opting out of allowing their medical data to be shared. In the two months from mid-May to mid-July, 60,000 more people withdrew their private information under a mechanism called the national data opt-out.

Doctors and patients’ groups are calling for Labour to exercise a break clause in Palantir’s seven-year contract. They cite its work with the Israeli military and Donald Trump’s ICE immigration agency and question the company’s claim to provide value for money.

highlights.title: Joey Barton to remain in custody until trial after bail application turned down
highlights.summary: Former footballer accused of attack outside golf club. His trial has been pushed back to March next year. The former footballer Joey Barton will remain in custody until his trial next year after a bail application was refused.
body: The 44-year-old had been due to stand trial at Liverpool crown court last week accused of causing grievous bodily harm with intent to Kevin Lynch, 51, at Fairway, Huyton, on 8 March. But on Wednesday the case was adjourned and put back to March next year.

Barton, wearing a grey zip-up fleece, appeared over video link from HMP Liverpool at a hearing on Monday, when Judge David Potter refused a renewed bail application. Barton nodded as the judge remanded him in custody in advance of a pre-trial hearing on 11 December.
His trial will take place exactly a year after the alleged assault, meaning the defendant, who was arrested shortly after the incident, will have spent 12 months on remand.

Barton is accused of carrying out the attack on Lynch after they had been drinking together at Huyton and Prescot golf club. Lynch, a former non-league football manager and founder of the special education school NexGen Academy, was said to have sustained serious injuries to an eye.

highlights.title: Why are so many people stealing from restaurants?
highlights.summary: About a quarter of British adults admit to having pilfered something from a pub or restaurant. Is it an Insta-fuelled craze, or just old-fashioned greed? Knives, candles, a toilet roll holder complete with screws and Rawlplugs – that’s just some of the stuff Michelin-starred restaurants in France…
body: A Québécois restaurateur complained about similar thefts in July – a picnic table, a painting and even the thermostat had been pinched – and British restaurateurs confirm it happens in the UK, too. Jan Ostle of Wilsons in Bristol told the BBC’s World at One that the mother-of-pearl spoons he uses to serve herb sorbet are a particular target: “Every few months I have to buy another 28.”

It’s an age-old, frequently aired story – all down to a sense of entitlement, or the desire for a souvenir, or booze-fuelled bravado – but it seems awfully retro. Wasn’t trousering a Conran restaurant ashtray a quintessential 90s petty crime? We’re supposed to be into “ experiences, not things ” now, and isn’t the whole point of posting a boring Instagram carousel of seven badly lit amuse -bouches to show everyone you’ve been somewhere fancy without stealing a side plate?

highlights.title: My Brief Summer Fling With Siri AI
highlights.summary: I was initially enamored with the beta version of Apple’s revamped smartphone assistant. As the full release approaches, I’ve forgotten Siri AI even exists.
body: When I first tested the developer beta of Apple's Siri AI by taking it as my tour guide around San Francisco, I was convinced the overhauled smartphone assistant would be an “ everything tool ” on the iPhone. The answers felt reliable enough and more helpful than previous versions of Siri. Also, the chatbot-style app for Siri felt very sleek, very Apple-y.

Over the next month, I kept experimenting with the Siri AI in the iOS 27 beta. The tool was quite powerful, especially with the personal context brought in by indexing the contents of my phone. Finding an ancient text message or photo has never been easier. Even so, my usage of the smartphone assistant slowly started tapering off.

It’s not that Siri AI isn’t better now. It is! This new version is quite the step change, which makes my reaction even more devastating. Siri AI isn’t revolutionizing how I interact with my phone the way I'd initially hoped, especially as an AI assistant built directly into the device and factoring in that Apple gives more thought to preserving my privacy than many other AI companies.

highlights.title: ‘Alpha Gang’ Review: Cate Blanchett, Léa Seydoux and Dave Bautista Get Stranded in a Sci-Fi Comedy That’s All Flash and Zero Substance
highlights.summary: Directed by David and Nathan Zellner ('Sasquatch Sunset'), the Telluride premiere follows aliens in '50s biker gear who've come to conquer Earth, but find newly human emotions get in the way.
body: Watching Alpha Gang, the new sci-fi comedy from Sasquatch Sunset filmmakers David and Nathan Zellner, it is very easy to imagine what a thrill it must have been to cook up the look of the thing.

It’s a striking hodgepodge of visual influences, and certainly an unusual one; I can’t think of another movie that climaxes with, essentially, medieval knights making their way through a Cold War nuclear bunker. But I also couldn’t quite tell you why this one does — or in fact why anything that happens in it happens at all. Premiering at Telluride, Alpha Gang is a mood board in search of a story.

It is at least possible to see that the script (written by both Zellners; only David is credited as director) intends to Say Something about what it means to be human in a time of great strife. The titular Alpha Gang are a star-studded sextet comprised of Léa Seydoux, Dave Bautista, Kelvin Harrison Jr., Lily-Rose Depp, Doona Bae and Riley Keough, their ID numbers (Alpha One, Alpha Two, etc.) going in that order. Like aliens from all over cinema, their mission here is to conquer, though they appear downright incurious about to what precise purpose.

highlights.title: Inside Parker Posey’s Venice Film Festival—From Sightseeing to Fabulous Fashions
highlights.summary: The star touched down in Venice for her film “Wild Horse Nine” this week. “I like looking like I’m showing up,” says Parker Posey.
body: Every year, the Venice Film Festival produces some of the most glitzy and glamorous red carpets outside of Hollywood—but Parker Posey is one of the few stars you can guarantee is having the most fun doing it all.

The actor took her own turn on the Lido to premiere her new film, Martin McDonagh’s Wild Horse Nine, which is one of the buzziest projects on the 2026 roster. (She co-stars alongside John Malkovich, Sam Rockwell, and Steve Buscemi.) “Venice is a magical city, and getting to celebrate Wild Horse Nine here is a treat,” says Posey of her whirlwind week at the enduringly chic festival. “I can’t not think of the Renaissance when I’m in Italy—the power of art and the presence of religion—all surrounded by water and reflections. Its baroque beauty is lush and bold!”

Before Posey began to think about attending the photo call and premiere—and, of course, dressing the part—she made sure to take some time for herself. After all, one must sightsee in the romantic, canaled Italian city. “I walked around at every break I’ve had over these past four days,” she says. “I’d find myself in churches lighting candles for my mom, who had surgery this week.”
